books.title: Wool: The Silo Saga, Book 1
books.author: Hugh Howey
books.blurb: Humanity's last survivors live in a giant underground silo, told the air outside is lethal and questions about it are forbidden. When a mechanic from the down deep is unexpectedly made sheriff, she starts pulling at threads the silo's rulers would rather stay buried. A slow-burn mystery wrapped in a dystopia that keeps re-justifying its own paranoia.

books.title: We Are Legion (We Are Bob): Bobiverse, Book 1
books.author: Dennis E. Taylor
books.blurb: Bob signs up to have his head cryogenically frozen, dies in a car accident, and wakes up a century later as a computer emulation drafted into piloting a self-replicating space probe. What follows is a funny, nerdy take on interstellar exploration where the hero keeps making copies of himself, each with a slightly different personality.

books.title: The Man in the High Castle
books.author: Philip K. Dick
books.blurb: An alternate 1962 in which Germany and Japan won World War II and split America between them. Dick is less interested in the war than in what occupation does to identity and truth, layering in a forbidden novel that imagines the Allies won. Strange, unsettling, and unlike any other alt-history.

books.title: Project Hail Mary
books.author: Andy Weir
books.blurb: A man wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of who he is or why he's there, and pieces together that he is humanity's last shot at stopping a microbe that is dimming the sun. Equal parts science puzzle and unlikely friendship story, and probably the most purely fun audiobook on this list.

books.title: One Second After
books.author: William R. Forstchen
books.blurb: An EMP attack instantly kills every modern electronic in America, and a small North Carolina town has to figure out food, medicine, and order as the country collapses around it. Grim and occasionally preachy, but it will change how you think about how fragile the systems we rely on really are.

books.title: Alas, Babylon
books.author: Pat Frank
books.blurb: Written in 1959 at the height of Cold War dread, it follows a small Florida town that survives a Soviet nuclear strike and has to rebuild a functioning community from scratch. One of the earliest and still one of the best entries in the post-apocalypse genre.

books.title: Recursion: A Novel
books.author: Blake Crouch
books.blurb: A detective investigates a syndrome that leaves people grieving lives they never lived, while a scientist builds a chair that can map and restore memories. Crouch turns a clever memory-travel premise into an escalating catastrophe that keeps topping itself.

books.title: Pines: Wayward Pines: 1
books.author: Blake Crouch
books.blurb: A Secret Service agent wakes up in a picture-perfect Idaho town he cannot leave, where the phones don't reach anyone and the residents seem to be performing their lives. The reveal behind Wayward Pines is genuinely audacious, and the ride there is fast.

books.title: Tempest: A Novel
books.author: Julie Cross
books.blurb: A nineteen-year-old discovers he can jump backward through time, and when his girlfriend is shot by mysterious agents, he retreats two years into the past to unravel who is hunting him. Light, fast YA time travel with a romance at its center.

books.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
books.blurb: From the dawn of man to a monolith orbiting Saturn, Clarke's novel follows an expedition accompanied by HAL, the ship's calmly homicidal computer. Written alongside the Kubrick film, the book explains what the movie leaves opaque, and the ideas about evolution and intelligence still land.

books.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
books.author: Robert A. Heinlein
books.blurb: Valentine Michael Smith, raised on Mars by Martians, arrives on Earth as an adult and views human religion, money, and jealousy as an alien would. Heinlein uses him to poke at every social convention of the 1960s. Dated in places, but a genuinely influential piece of science fiction.

books.title: Seveneves: A Novel
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.blurb: The moon breaks apart, and humanity has two years before the fragments turn the sky into fire. Stephenson spends the first two-thirds on the desperate engineering scramble to get a fragment of civilization into orbit, then jumps five thousand years to see what those choices became. Dense, technical, and epic in the true sense.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Cixin Liu
books.blurb: During China's Cultural Revolution, a physicist makes contact with an alien civilization whose home world is being torn apart by three suns, and quietly invites them to Earth. The first book of a trilogy that scales from historical trauma to some of the biggest ideas in modern science fiction.

books.title: Matched: Book 1
books.author: Ally Condie
books.blurb: In the Society, officials decide who you love, where you work, and when you die. Cassia trusts the system until the wrong face flashes on her matching screen for an instant. YA dystopia focused on quiet control rather than spectacle.

books.title: Uglies: Uglies, Book 1
books.author: Scott Westerfeld
books.blurb: Everyone gets an operation at sixteen that makes them beautiful, and Tally can't wait for hers until she meets someone who plans to refuse it. A YA series with a sharper point than its premise suggests, about what conformity costs and who benefits from it.

books.title: The Handmaid's Tale
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.blurb: In the Republic of Gilead, a theocratic coup has stripped women of property, reading, and their own names, and Offred survives as a handmaid whose only sanctioned purpose is bearing children. Atwood claims she invented nothing that hasn't happened somewhere, which is exactly what makes it linger.

books.title: 11-22-63: A Novel
books.author: Stephen King
books.blurb: A high school teacher finds a portal to 1958 and takes on the ultimate what-if: living in the past for five years to stop the Kennedy assassination. King's best latter-day book, as much a love story about a vanished America as a time-travel thriller. The past, he warns, does not want to be changed.

books.title: Haunted
books.author: Chuck Palahniuk
books.blurb: Writers answer an ad for a secluded retreat and end up locked in a decaying theater, each telling the story that ruined them while the group sabotages its own survival for the sake of a better narrative. Contains some of the most notorious short stories Palahniuk has written. Not for the faint of stomach.

books.title: I Am Legend
books.author: Richard Matheson
books.blurb: Robert Neville is the last man in a world where a plague has turned everyone else into vampiric creatures, and he spends his days hunting them and his nights barricaded in his house. The ending inverts the entire genre, and the title is the punchline.

books.title: Sphere
books.author: Michael Crichton
books.blurb: A psychologist is helicoptered to the middle of the Pacific, where the Navy has found a spacecraft on the ocean floor that appears to be three hundred years old. What the team finds inside starts granting wishes nobody should have. Crichton at his claustrophobic best.

books.title: Timeline: A Novel
books.author: Michael Crichton
books.blurb: Archaeologists use quantum technology to travel to fourteenth-century France, where the past turns out to be considerably better armed than expected. A historical adventure wearing a sci-fi costume, with Crichton's usual knack for making the science feel plausible.

books.title: Jurassic Park: A Novel
books.author: Michael Crichton
books.blurb: A billionaire clones dinosaurs from fossilized DNA and builds a theme park around them, confident that the systems keeping them contained cannot fail. The book is darker and more cynical than the movie, and its argument about complexity and hubris holds up better every year.

books.title: Inheritance Games
books.author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
books.blurb: A broke teenager inherits billions from a stranger, on the condition that she move into his mansion alongside the family he disinherited, including four grandsons who want to know why. A puzzle-box YA mystery built on riddles and games.

books.title: Under the Dome: A Novel
books.author: Stephen King
books.blurb: An invisible barrier seals a Maine town off from the world in an instant, and the real horror turns out to be the local politician who sees opportunity in the crisis. King uses the sci-fi premise as a pressure cooker for a study of small-town power.

books.title: The Institute: A Novel
books.author: Stephen King
books.blurb: Children with faint psychic abilities are kidnapped and warehoused in a facility that harvests what's in their heads, until one unusually smart boy arrives. Classic King territory: institutional evil, resilient kids, and the slow assembly of a rebellion.

books.title: The Most Dangerous Game
books.author: Richard Connell
books.blurb: A big-game hunter falls off a yacht and swims to an island owned by a Russian aristocrat who has grown bored of hunting animals. The 1924 short story that launched a hundred imitations, still tense at under an hour.

books.title: Flesh: A Novel
books.author: David Szalay
books.blurb: A Hungarian teenager drifts from a small apartment block to the army to the orbit of London's ultra-rich, his life shaped by events he barely speaks about. Szalay tells an entire life in spare, flat prose where everything important happens between the lines. Winner of the Booker Prize.

books.title: Fight Club
books.author: Chuck Palahniuk
books.blurb: An insomniac office drone meets Tyler Durden, and together they invent a bare-knuckle ritual that metastasizes into something much bigger and stranger. The novel is leaner and meaner than the film, a satire of consumer masculinity that got adopted by the people it was mocking.

books.title: The Overstory
books.author: Richard Powers
books.blurb: Nine strangers, each marked by a tree somewhere in their past, converge on the fight over America's last old-growth forests. Powers makes trees feel like characters operating on a timescale we can barely perceive. A Pulitzer winner that genuinely changes how you look out a window.

books.title: Forrest Gump
books.author: Winston Groom
books.blurb: The novel behind the movie is rougher, raunchier, and stranger: Forrest goes to space, plays chess professionally, and wrestles under the name The Dunce. Groom's hero narrates his improbable sweep through American history with the same guileless deadpan throughout.

books.title: North Woods: A Novel
books.author: Daniel Mason
books.blurb: A single plot of land in New England, followed for four centuries through everyone and everything that inhabits it: colonists, an apple grower, painters, ghosts, a mountain lion. A novel about time and place where the house is the protagonist. Quietly brilliant.

books.title: Survivor
books.author: Chuck Palahniuk
books.blurb: The last member of a death cult dictates his life story into the black box of a hijacked 747 as it runs out of fuel. Palahniuk's satire of celebrity religion, self-help culture, and manufactured messiahs, told in chapters that count down to impact.

books.title: The Alchemist: A Fable About Following Your Dream
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.blurb: A young Andalusian shepherd sells his flock to chase a recurring dream about treasure at the Egyptian pyramids, and the journey becomes the point. A simple fable about listening to what you actually want. You'll either find it profound or slight; either way it takes an afternoon.

books.title: Choke
books.author: Chuck Palahniuk
books.blurb: A med-school dropout finances his mother's care by pretending to choke in restaurants, letting strangers save him and then letting them feel responsible for his life. Palahniuk's twisted take on addiction, con artistry, and the need to be needed.

books.title: The Bonfire of the Vanities
books.author: Tom Wolfe
books.blurb: A Wall Street bond trader takes a wrong turn in the Bronx, and the resulting accident becomes fuel for prosecutors, activists, and tabloids that each need him to be a villain. Wolfe's giant satire of 1980s New York, where every character is performing for an audience.

books.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest: 50th Anniversary Edition
books.author: Ken Kesey
books.blurb: Randle McMurphy fakes insanity to serve his sentence in a psychiatric hospital and collides with Nurse Ratched, who runs the ward through procedure and quiet humiliation. A novel about institutional control that reads as fresh as the day it was published.

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.author: Harper Lee
books.blurb: Scout Finch watches her father defend a Black man falsely accused in Depression-era Alabama, and learns how her town actually works. A great American classic that earns the label, told through a child's eyes without childishness.

books.title: The Midnight Library: A GMA Book Club Pick (A Novel)
books.author: Matt Haig
books.blurb: Between life and death sits a library where every book is a version of your life had you chosen differently, and Nora Seed gets to try them. A gentle thought experiment about regret that wears its philosophy lightly.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.blurb: Jay Gatsby builds a fortune and a mansion across the bay from the woman he lost, believing money can buy back the past. Fitzgerald's short, perfect novel about reinvention and the hollowness underneath it. The Gyllenhaal narration is excellent.

books.title: Infinite Jest
books.author: David Foster Wallace
books.blurb: Set between a tennis academy and a halfway house, it orbits a film so entertaining that anyone who watches it loses the will to do anything else. Wallace's enormous novel about addiction and entertainment demands real commitment and repays a surprising amount of it.

books.title: Palo Alto: Stories
books.author: James Franco
books.blurb: Linked short stories about aimless Palo Alto teenagers drifting through parties, cruelty, and boredom in the shadow of a town known for ambition. Franco draws on his own adolescence here; bleak, but it captures something true about growing up numb in a wealthy suburb.

books.title: The Last Days of Night: A Novel
books.author: Graham Moore
books.blurb: A young lawyer takes on Thomas Edison on behalf of George Westinghouse in the patent war over the light bulb, with Nikola Tesla wandering brilliantly through the middle. A fictionalized but well-researched account of the current wars, paced like a thriller.

books.title: 1929: Inside the Greatest Crash in Wall Street History--and How It Shattered a Nation
books.author: Andrew Ross Sorkin
books.blurb: Sorkin reconstructs the crash of 1929 through the bankers, promoters, and politicians who inflated the bubble and then scrambled to survive it. Reads like a novel and doubles as a warning: every generation believes it has outgrown the mistakes this book documents.

books.title: The Great Mental Models, Volume 4: Economics and Art
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.blurb: The fourth Mental Models volume pulls its ideas from economics and art: incentives, scarcity, supply and demand, audience, and framing. Like the whole series, it's a toolbox of ways to think rather than a set of answers.

books.title: Systems and Mathematics: The Great Mental Models, Volume 3
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.blurb: Feedback loops, equilibrium, compounding, distributions, and the other load-bearing ideas from systems thinking and math, explained without requiring any of the underlying technical machinery. Volume 3 of the Mental Models series.

books.title: Poor Charlie’s Almanack: The Essential Wit and Wisdom of Charles T. Munger
books.author: Charles T. Munger
books.blurb: A compendium of Charlie Munger's talks, most famously The Psychology of Human Misjudgment, stitched together with his biography and his one-liners. The core idea: collect the big ideas from every discipline and use them as a checklist against your own stupidity.

books.title: $100M Offers: How to Make Offers So Good People Feel Stupid Saying No
books.author: Alex Hormozi
books.blurb: Hormozi's formula for building an offer so lopsided with value that saying no feels foolish: raise the dream outcome, raise certainty, cut time and effort, then stack guarantees. Direct, tactical, and refreshingly free of filler.

books.title: Liar's Poker: Rising Through the Wreckage on Wall Street
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.blurb: Lewis's memoir of stumbling into Salomon Brothers in the mid-1980s, where trainees were graded on nerve and mortgage traders threw phones. He wrote it as a warning about Wall Street; a generation read it as a recruiting brochure.

books.title: Way of the Wolf: Straight Line Selling: Master the Art of Persuasion, Influence, and Success
books.author: Jordan Belfort
books.blurb: Jordan Belfort teaches the Straight Line, the sales system he drilled into brokers: control tone, build certainty in the product, the salesperson, and the firm, and keep the conversation on a line toward the close. Read it as a masterclass or as a warning; it works as both.

books.title: Freakonomics: Revised Edition
books.author: Steven D. Levitt
books.blurb: Levitt and Dubner apply an economist's toolkit to cheating teachers, sumo wrestlers, drug-gang finances, and baby names, always hunting for the incentive underneath the behavior. The book that made thinking in incentives mainstream.

books.title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
books.author: Thomas Piketty
books.blurb: Piketty assembles two centuries of data across twenty countries to argue that returns on capital tend to outrun economic growth, concentrating wealth absent deliberate intervention. Long and data-dense, but the argument reshaped how inequality gets debated.

books.title: Flash Boys: A Wall Street Revolt
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.blurb: A small group of traders discovers that the US stock market has been quietly rewired so that high-frequency firms can see orders microseconds early, and decides to build an exchange that makes the advantage worthless. Lewis at his best: a rigged system explained through the people who refused to accept it.

books.title: The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.blurb: The financial crisis of 2008 told through the handful of misfits who read the mortgage bonds, realized the system was insolvent, and bet against it while being laughed at. Nobody explains complex finance through character better than Lewis.

books.title: The Accidental Billionaires: The Founding of Facebook: A Tale of Sex, Money, Genius and Betrayal
books.author: Ben Mezrich
books.blurb: Mezrich's dramatized account of Facebook's founding at Harvard: the deal between Zuckerberg and Saverin, the Winklevoss dispute, and the friendship that dissolved as the company grew. The book that became The Social Network. Take the dialogue with salt; the arc is real.

books.title: Fundraising
books.author: Ryan Breslow
books.blurb: Breslow, who raised at a multi-billion valuation for Bolt, compresses the startup fundraising playbook into about an hour: run a tight process, create parallel demand, control the narrative, and understand what investors actually optimize for. Short enough to re-listen before every raise.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer: 20th Anniversary Edition, 2nd Edition: Your Journey to Mastery
books.author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
books.blurb: The rare software book that survives decades: tracer bullets, the DRY principle, fixing broken windows, and owning your craft. The 20th-anniversary rewrite keeps it current. If you write code for a living, this one earns its place.

books.title: Careless People: A Cautionary Tale of Power, Greed, and Lost Idealism
books.author: Sarah Wynn-Williams
books.blurb: A former Facebook policy executive describes seven years inside the company's leadership, from diplomatic absurdities to decisions with body counts attached. Meta tried to suppress the book, which tells you something. Scathing, funny, and sad in equal measure.

books.title: Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup
books.author: John Carreyrou
books.blurb: Carreyrou's investigation of Theranos, the blood-testing startup that ran on fake demos and intimidation while putting patients at risk. The definitive account of how far charisma and a good story can carry a fraud in the Valley, and what it takes to stop one.

books.title: The New New Thing: A Silicon Valley Story
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.blurb: Lewis profiles Jim Clark, the restless founder of Silicon Graphics, Netscape, and Healtheon, as he chases the next big thing on a computerized sailboat. A snapshot of the exact moment Silicon Valley figured out that stories about the future could mint billions.

books.title: Brotopia: Breaking Up the Boys' Club of Silicon Valley
books.author: Emily Chang
books.blurb: Chang traces how an industry that once employed a large share of women programmers narrowed into a boys' club, from the PDP-era personality test that screened for antisocial men to the modern funding gap. Reported, specific, and hard to wave away.

books.title: How to Rule the World: An Education in Power at Stanford University
books.author: Theo Baker
books.blurb: Baker, the youngest Polk Award winner, spent his Stanford years investigating his own university: its president's flawed research, its ties to money and power, and the machinery that grooms students for influence. A sharp inside look at the institution that feeds Silicon Valley.

books.title: Hackers & Painters: Big Ideas from the Computer Age
books.author: Paul Graham
books.blurb: Graham's essays on why nerds lose at high school and win afterward, why great hackers resemble artists more than engineers, and how wealth actually gets created. Opinionated in the best way; half the essays will convince you and the other half will start arguments.

books.title: Secrets of Sand Hill Road: Venture Capital and How to Get It
books.author: Scott Kupor
books.blurb: Kupor, a longtime Andreessen Horowitz partner, explains venture capital from the inside: how funds work, what LPs expect, how term sheets actually allocate power, and what that means when you're the founder across the table. The clearest single primer on the VC game.

books.title: Chaos Monkeys: Obscene Fortune and Random Failure in Silicon Valley
books.author: Antonio Garcia Martinez
books.blurb: Garcia Martinez sells his startup, lands at Facebook, and narrates the ads-platform wars with the candor of a man burning every bridge behind him. Cynical, score-settling, and one of the most honest books about how the money side of the Valley actually operates.

books.title: Disrupted: My Misadventure in the Start-Up Bubble
books.author: Dan Lyons
books.blurb: Lyons, laid off from Newsweek at 52, joins a hot marketing startup and finds a candy-wall cult of mandatory positivity where employees are graded on culture fit and fired by euphemism. The funniest book written about startup life, with a real critique underneath.

books.title: The Genome Odyssey: Medical Mysteries and the Incredible Quest to Solve Them
books.author: Euan Angus Ashley
books.blurb: Ashley, a Stanford cardiologist, tells the stories of patients whose mystery diseases were finally cracked by genome sequencing, and of the teams racing to make that routine. Medicine's shift from symptoms to code, told through actual cases.

books.title: Physics, Chemistry, and Biology: The Great Mental Models, Volume 2
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.blurb: Relativity, reciprocity, thermodynamics, inertia, evolution, and other bedrock scientific concepts repurposed as thinking tools for everyday decisions. Volume 2 of the Mental Models series.

books.title: The Demon-Haunted World: Science as a Candle in the Dark
books.author: Carl Sagan
books.blurb: Sagan's defense of skepticism as a survival skill, complete with his baloney-detection kit for evaluating claims. Written in 1995, it predicted the misinformation era with uncomfortable precision. The chapter on the dragon in the garage alone is worth the book.

books.title: The Selfish Gene
books.author: Richard Dawkins
books.blurb: Dawkins reframes evolution from the gene's point of view: bodies are vehicles genes build to copy themselves, and altruism, parenting, and cooperation all fall out of that arithmetic. One of the rare science books that permanently rearranges how you see living things.

books.title: Genome: The Autobiography of a Species in 23 Chapters
books.author: Matt Ridley
books.blurb: Ridley takes one newly-mapped gene from each of our 23 chromosomes and uses it to tell a story: about disease, intelligence, personality, history, and the misuses of genetic ideas. A tour of what the genome does and doesn't determine.

books.title: The Great Influenza: The Epic Story of the Deadliest Plague in History
books.author: John M. Barry
books.blurb: The 1918 flu killed more people than the World War it rode in on, and Barry tracks both the virus and the young American science establishment racing to understand it. The parallels to modern pandemics need no pointing out.

books.title: The Interpretation of Dreams
books.author: Sigmund Freud
books.blurb: Freud's argument that dreams are disguised wish fulfillment, and the book that introduced the unconscious to the general public. Much of it hasn't survived scientifically, but its influence on how we talk about the mind is everywhere, and the case studies remain fascinating.

books.title: The Great Mental Models: General Thinking Concepts
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.blurb: The first Mental Models volume: the map is not the territory, circle of competence, inversion, second-order thinking, Occam's razor. A starter kit for reasoning that transfers to almost any decision.

books.title: Wanting: The Power of Mimetic Desire in Everyday Life
books.author: Luke Burgis
books.blurb: Girard's theory of mimetic desire, made practical: we don't want things so much as we copy the wanting of others, which explains fashion, rivalry, bubbles, and career envy. Burgis's book is the accessible on-ramp to an idea that explains an unsettling amount of behavior.

books.title: Determined: A Science of Life Without Free Will
books.author: Robert M. Sapolsky
books.blurb: Sapolsky follows the biology of behavior all the way down and concludes there is no room left for free will: every choice is the output of genes, environment, and the moment before. Whether or not you accept the conclusion, the argument is formidable and the implications for blame and punishment are serious.

books.title: The Sociopath Next Door
books.author: Martha Stout
books.blurb: Stout's claim: roughly one in twenty-five people has no conscience, and most of them are not killers but bosses, partners, and neighbors who play by entirely different rules. Useful as a field guide to manipulation, whatever you make of the prevalence numbers.

books.title: The Undoing Project: A Friendship That Changed Our Minds
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.blurb: The friendship between Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky, whose arguments with each other produced the science of cognitive bias. Lewis makes the relationship the story: two opposite men who thought better together than anyone thought alone, until the collaboration curdled.

books.title: Rethinking Narcissism: The Bad - and Surprising Good - About Feeling Special
books.author: Dr. Craig Malkin
books.blurb: Malkin treats narcissism as a spectrum everyone sits on: too much is destructive, but so is too little. Comes with tools for spotting the difference between healthy confidence and exploitation, and for dealing with the people at the far end.

books.title: Predictably Irrational: The Hidden Forces That Shape Our Decisions
books.author: Dan Ariely
books.blurb: Ariely's experiments on why we overvalue free things, why decoy prices work, why we cheat a little but not a lot, and why expectations change experience. The cheerful, readable introduction to how systematically weird human decisions are.

books.title: Influence: Science and Practice, ePub, 5th Edition
books.author: Robert B. Cialdini
books.blurb: Cialdini's six levers of persuasion: reciprocity, commitment, social proof, liking, authority, and scarcity, each documented through experiments and through the compliance professionals who weaponize them. Read it to persuade or to notice when it's being done to you.

books.title: The Game: Penetrating the Secret Society of Pickup Artists
books.author: Neil Strauss
books.blurb: Strauss embeds with the pickup-artist underground and becomes its star pupil, then watches the community consume itself. Half how-to, half cautionary tale about what happens when you optimize for seduction and call it self-improvement.

books.title: ADD in Intimate Relationships: A Comprehensive Guide for Couples
books.author: Daniel G. Amen
books.blurb: Amen on how attention deficit disorder shows up inside couples: the forgetfulness, conflict-seeking, and overwhelm that get misread as not caring. Practical guidance for both partners, from a clinic that has seen thousands of these cases.

books.title: Infidelity: Why Men and Women Cheat
books.author: Kenneth Paul Rosenberg
books.blurb: Rosenberg, a psychiatrist, walks through what brain science says about desire, attachment, and why people cheat, and how couples survive it or don't. Less moralizing than the title suggests; more interested in mechanisms than blame.

books.title: The State of Affairs: Rethinking Infidelity
books.author: Esther Perel
books.blurb: Perel's contrarian look at infidelity: affairs are as much about the self you miss as the partner you betray, and recovery is possible but never symmetric. Uncomfortable, humane, and full of lines you'll want to argue with out loud.

books.title: The Truth
books.author: Neil Strauss
books.blurb: After The Game blows up his life, Strauss checks into rehab for sex addiction and road-tests every alternative to monogamy he can find before circling back to what he actually wants. The rare sequel that undermines its predecessor honestly.

books.title: Modern Romance: An Investigation
books.author: Aziz Ansari
books.blurb: Ansari teams up with a sociologist to study how smartphones rewired dating: infinite options, texting games, and the paradox of choice applied to people. Genuinely researched and genuinely funny, especially in the author-read audio.

books.title: The Ethical Slut: A Practical Guide to Polyamory, Open Relationships, & Other Adventures
books.author: Janet W. Hardy
books.blurb: The standard reference on consensual non-monogamy: jealousy, agreements, communication, and the practical mechanics of relationships that don't follow the default script. Whatever your arrangement, its chapters on honest negotiation apply.

books.title: Mating in Captivity: Reconciling the Erotic & the Domestic
books.author: Esther Perel
books.blurb: Perel's core paradox: love wants closeness and safety, desire wants distance and mystery, and long-term couples have to hold both. The book that made her famous, and still the sharpest statement of the problem.

books.title: The Theory of the Leisure Class
books.author: Thorstein Veblen
books.blurb: Veblen, writing in 1899, coins conspicuous consumption: the rich signal status by wasting time and money visibly, and everyone below imitates them. Swap carriages for watches and yachts and the analysis reads like it was written this year.

books.title: Caste: The Origins of Our Discontents
books.author: Isabel Wilkerson
books.blurb: Wilkerson argues America's racial hierarchy works like a caste system, with the same machinery of rank, purity rules, and enforcement found in India and Nazi Germany. Whatever you conclude, the historical reporting is meticulous and the framework is hard to unsee.

books.title: The Better Angels of Our Nature: Why Violence Has Declined
books.author: Steven Pinker
books.blurb: Pinker marshals centuries of data to argue that violence of every kind has declined, and tries to explain why: states, commerce, literacy, reason. A genuinely optimistic book that forces you to check your instincts against the numbers.

books.title: The Rational Optimist: How Prosperity Evolves
books.author: Matt Ridley
books.blurb: Ridley's case that exchange and specialization are humanity's engine: when ideas can meet and mate, prosperity compounds. A deliberate antidote to doom, and a useful frame even where you think he's too sunny.

books.title: Gang Leader for a Day: A Rogue Sociologist Takes to the Streets
books.author: Sudhir Venkatesh
books.blurb: A sociology grad student walks into a Chicago housing project with a survey and ends up spending years inside a crack-selling gang, learning its org chart, wages, and politics. The fieldwork behind Freakonomics' most famous chapter, with all the texture the summary left out.

books.title: Bobos in Paradise: The New Upper Class and How They Got There
books.author: David Brooks
books.blurb: Brooks anatomizes the bourgeois bohemians: the educated class that fused sixties counterculture with eighties ambition and made spending virtuous. Written in 2000, it accidentally described the next twenty-five years of upscale taste.

books.title: Old Money: The Mythology of Wealth in America
books.author: Nelson Aldrich
books.blurb: Aldrich, himself old money, examines America's inherited-wealth class from the inside: its codes, guilt, institutions, and its uneasy relationship with the newly rich. An odd, thoughtful book on a subject Americans pretend not to have.

books.title: White Trash: The 400-Year Untold History of Class in America
books.author: Nancy Isenberg
books.blurb: Isenberg traces four hundred years of America's white underclass, from colonial waste people to hillbillies to trailer parks, and shows how much of national politics is class contempt wearing other costumes. A history that explains more current events than it should.

books.title: Very Important People: Status and Beauty in the Global Party Circuit
books.author: Ashley Mears
books.blurb: Mears, a sociologist and former model, spends eighteen months inside the global VIP party circuit documenting how beauty is recruited, comped, and spent to signal men's status. A sharp ethnography of an economy everyone senses and nobody names.

books.title: Troubled: The Failed Promise of America’s Behavioral Treatment Programs
books.author: Kenneth R. Rosen
books.blurb: Rosen, who survived four programs himself, investigates the tough-love industry for troubled teens: wilderness camps, boot camps, and residential facilities where discipline shades into abuse. Reporting that helped force a reckoning with an industry parents trusted blind.

books.title: What Would Mrs. Astor Do?: The Essential Guide to the Manners and Mores of the Gilded Age (Washington Mews Books, Book 5)
books.author: Cecelia Tichi
books.blurb: A guided tour of Gilded Age New York's social machinery: calling cards, opera boxes, seating charts, and the four hundred people who mattered, ruled over by Caroline Astor. Frothy on the surface, but sneakily good on how status systems actually operate.

books.title: King of Kings: The Fall of the Shah and the Revolution That Forged Modern Iran
books.author: Scott Anderson
books.blurb: Anderson reconstructs the Iranian Revolution through the Americans and Iranians who lived it, showing how the Shah's regime rotted from within while Washington saw only its own reflection. The best single explanation of how 1979 still shapes the region.

books.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.blurb: Harari's sweep from forager bands to empires to algorithms, built on one idea: humans dominate because we cooperate around shared fictions like money, nations, and gods. Parts are contested and parts are glib, but as a frame for thinking about our species it's unmatched.

books.title: Israel: A Concise History of a Nation Reborn
books.author: Daniel Gordis
books.blurb: Gordis covers Israel from the earliest Zionist arguments through statehood, wars, and modern politics, focusing on the ideas the country was built to answer. Sympathetic but not uncritical, and the most efficient single-volume introduction available.

books.title: Americana: A 400-Year History of American Capitalism
books.author: Bhu Srinivasan
books.blurb: Srinivasan tells American history through its businesses: tobacco, canals, railroads, radio, venture capital, each chapter an industry that remade the country. Four hundred years of capitalism, told as a story rather than a lecture.

books.title: The Great Earthquake and Firestorms of 1906: How San Francisco Nearly Destroyed Itself
books.author: Philip L. Fradkin
books.blurb: The 1906 earthquake broke San Francisco, but the fires and the decisions that followed did most of the destroying. Fradkin is unsparing about the officials who dynamited neighborhoods, lied about deaths, and rebuilt on the same fault lines.

books.title: Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World
books.author: Malcolm Harris
books.blurb: Harris's massive, combative history argues that Palo Alto perfected a system for extracting profit from talent, from Stanford's horse farm through eugenics, defense money, and startups. Openly polemical, but full of history the Valley prefers to forget. Read it alongside the boosters.

books.title: The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test
books.author: Tom Wolfe
books.blurb: Wolfe rides with Ken Kesey and the Merry Pranksters as they drive a painted bus across America dosing themselves and inventing the acid-test parties that became the counterculture. New Journalism at full volume; you can hear the sixties turning.

books.title: Countdown 1945: The Extraordinary Story of the Atomic Bomb and the 116 Days That Changed the World
books.author: Chris Wallace
books.blurb: Wallace counts down the 116 days from Roosevelt's death to Hiroshima through Truman, the Los Alamos scientists, and the crew of the Enola Gay. A propulsive account of the decision that opened the nuclear age.

books.title: The Pioneers: The Heroic Story of the Settlers Who Brought the American Ideal West
books.author: David McCullough
books.blurb: McCullough follows the New Englanders who settled the Ohio territory, carrying with them a ban on slavery and a mania for schools. A smaller, quieter story than his presidential biographies, about the unglamorous work of building institutions from mud.

books.title: Nuclear War: A Scenario
books.author: Annie Jacobsen
books.blurb: Jacobsen walks through a nuclear exchange minute by minute, from launch detection to the collapse of everything after, based on interviews with the people who built the plans. The scariest book on this list by a wide margin, and it's all sourced.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.author: Tom Wolfe
books.blurb: Wolfe's account of the test pilots and Mercury astronauts, and of the unspoken code of courage they measured each other against. The best book ever written about American machismo pointed at the sky.

books.title: The Art of War
books.author: Sun Tzu
books.blurb: Sun Tzu's 2,500-year-old manual on winning conflicts, ideally without fighting them: deception, positioning, timing, and knowing yourself and your enemy. Short enough to finish in a sitting and vague enough to apply to everything, which is why everyone from generals to founders quotes it.

books.title: Misquoting Jesus
books.author: Bart D. Ehrman
books.blurb: Ehrman, a textual scholar who began as an evangelical, explains how the New Testament was copied by hand for centuries and what the accumulated changes mean, from slips of the pen to deliberate edits. A calm, scholarly book about an explosive subject.

books.title: The Fort Bragg Cartel: Drug Trafficking and Murder in the Special Forces
books.author: Seth Harp
books.blurb: Harp investigates a string of unexplained deaths at Fort Bragg and finds Special Forces soldiers moving drugs, a base flooded with fentanyl, and an Army with no appetite for looking closely. Reporting that reads like a thriller and lands like an indictment.

books.title: Helter Skelter: The True Story of the Manson Murders
books.author: Vincent Bugliosi
books.blurb: The Manson murders told by the man who prosecuted them. Bugliosi walks through the crimes, the investigation's fumbles, and the trial where he had to convince a jury that Manson killed through obedience. The bestselling true crime book ever written, and it earns it.

books.title: American Kingpin: The Epic Hunt for the Criminal Mastermind Behind the Silk Road
books.author: Nick Bilton
books.blurb: Ross Ulbricht built the Silk Road, an eBay for drugs run from laptops in coffee shops, and became a libertarian folk hero while ordering hits he thought he was paying for. Bilton turns the hunt for the Dread Pirate Roberts into a genuine page-turner.

books.title: Who Killed Jane Stanford?: A Gilded Age Tale of Murder, Deceit, Spirits and the Birth of a University
books.author: Richard White
books.blurb: Stanford University's co-founder was poisoned with strychnine in 1905, and the university's first president led the effort to declare it natural causes. White, a Stanford historian, reopens the case and names a culprit. Gilded Age murder plus institutional cover-up.

books.title: Mindhunter: Inside the FBI's Elite Serial Crime Unit
books.author: John E. Douglas
books.blurb: Douglas spent his FBI career interviewing serial killers and turning what he heard into criminal profiling. The memoir behind the Netflix series, equal parts casework and the cost of spending decades inside the worst minds available.

books.title: American Radical: Inside the World of an Undercover Muslim FBI Agent
books.author: Tamer Elnoury
books.blurb: An undercover FBI agent, himself a devout Muslim, spends years inside terror plots, wearing a wire while extremists debate targets. Elnoury's double life raises hard questions about faith, loyalty, and what counterterrorism actually looks like from inside.

books.title: Billion Dollar Whale
books.author: Bradley Hope
books.blurb: Jho Low siphoned billions from a Malaysian sovereign fund and spent it on Hollywood, superyachts, and Wolf of Wall Street financing while Goldman Sachs collected fees. A heist story where the getaway car is the global financial system.

books.title: Spare
books.author: Prince Harry The Duke of Sussex
books.blurb: Prince Harry on growing up as the designated backup: his mother's death, the tabloid machine, Afghanistan, and the family rupture that followed his exit. Whatever you think of the institution, it's a startlingly candid book, and his narration makes it more so.

books.title: Source Code: My Beginnings
books.author: Bill Gates
books.blurb: Bill Gates on his beginnings: a restless kid in Seattle, a lucky terminal, thousands of hours of code, and the decision to leave Harvard and bet on software. It ends before Microsoft gets big, which is exactly why it works; it's about how the machine got built.

books.title: Vanderbilt: The Rise and Fall of an American Dynasty
books.author: Anderson Cooper, Katherine Howe
books.blurb: Cooper, the family's most famous living descendant, teams with a historian to trace the Commodore's ruthless fortune and the gilded generations that spent it into legend and then into nothing. A dynasty story told with the access of an insider and the distance of a journalist.

books.title: The Trading Game: A Confession
books.author: Gary Stevenson
books.blurb: Stevenson grows up poor in East London, wins a Citibank trading seat by being better at a card game, and becomes one of the bank's most profitable traders by betting the economy would stay broken. Then the money stops meaning anything. The most honest book about trading in years.

books.title: Einstein: His Life and Universe
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.blurb: Isaacson's full portrait: the patent clerk who rewrote physics, the celebrity who couldn't manage his own family, the refugee who watched his equations become weapons. Makes the science graspable and the man complicated.

books.title: Elon Musk
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.blurb: Isaacson shadowed Musk for two years across Tesla, SpaceX, and the Twitter purchase, and the result is the fullest picture yet of the demon-mode management style and the output and damage it produces. Neither hagiography nor hit piece.

books.title: King: A Life
books.author: Jonathan Eig
books.blurb: Eig's biography of Martin Luther King Jr. uses newly released FBI files and fresh interviews to recover the man from the monument: brilliant, depressive, surveilled, and braver than the sanitized version suggests. The definitive modern King biography.

books.title: Paris: The Memoir
books.author: Paris Hilton
books.blurb: Paris Hilton on inventing the famous-for-being-famous playbook, and on the abusive troubled-teen facilities her parents sent her to, which she has since campaigned against. Far more substance than the brand implies.

books.title: Benjamin Franklin: An American Life
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.blurb: Printer, scientist, diplomat, founder: Isaacson's Franklin is the most approachable of the founders, a self-made operator whose pragmatism and humor built institutions we still use. The best single door into the founding generation.

books.title: Washington: A Life
books.author: Ron Chernow
books.blurb: Chernow's cradle-to-grave Washington: ambitious, thin-skinned, physically fearless, and acutely aware that everything he did set precedent. The book's achievement is making the marble statue back into a striving, calculating man.

books.title: Leland Stanford: The Life and Legacy of the Railroad Executive Who Became California's Governor and the West's Most Famous Robber Baron
books.author: Charles River Editors
books.blurb: A short biography of the railroad baron and politician who built a fortune on the transcontinental line and turned grief for his son into a university. Useful context for anyone living in the world Stanford money built.

books.title: Will
books.author: Will Smith
books.blurb: Will Smith tells his story as a series of performances: the fearful kid in Philadelphia, the rapper, the biggest movie star alive, and the husband and father performing happiness. Co-written with Mark Manson, unexpectedly raw, and terrific in audio.

books.title: A Promised Land
books.author: Barack Obama
books.blurb: Obama's first presidential volume, from Chicago organizing through the bin Laden raid, with long, candid detours into how the sausage actually gets made. He's a genuine writer, and his narration turns it into forty hours of fireside explanation.

books.title: Washington's End: The Final Years and Forgotten Struggle
books.author: Jonathan Horn
books.blurb: Horn picks up where most Washington biographies stop: the awkward final years after the presidency, watching the republic he built fracture into parties while he worried about his legacy and his will. A study of what it means to actually give up power.

books.title: Picking Up: On the Streets and Behind the Trucks with the Sanitation Workers of New York City
books.author: Robin Nagle
books.blurb: Nagle, anthropologist-in-residence at New York's sanitation department, rides the trucks and documents the invisible system that keeps a city from drowning in its own trash. You will never see a garbage truck the same way.

books.title: Thank You for My Service
books.author: Mat Best
books.blurb: Army Ranger turned internet personality Mat Best on deployments, dark humor as a survival mechanism, and building a business with veterans afterward. Profane, funny, and more thoughtful about war than it pretends to be.

books.title: My Own Words
books.author: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
books.blurb: Ruth Bader Ginsburg in her own writing: briefs, bench announcements, speeches on dissent and equality, with context from her biographers. Less a memoir than a documentary record of how she argued the world into changing.

books.title: Born a Crime: Stories from a South African Childhood
books.author: Trevor Noah
books.blurb: Trevor Noah's childhood under apartheid, where his existence as a mixed child was literally illegal, raised by a fearless religious mother. Funny and harrowing in the same paragraph. The audio, in Noah's own voices, is the definitive version.

books.title: 21: Bringing Down the House: The Inside Story of Six M.I.T. Students Who Took Vegas for Millions
books.author: Ben Mezrich
books.blurb: Six MIT students turn card counting into a business, flying to Vegas with hundreds of thousands strapped to their bodies until the casinos catch on. Mezrich's dramatized but irresistible account of math beating the house.

books.title: Leonardo da Vinci
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.blurb: Isaacson reads Leonardo through his notebooks: the to-do lists, dissections, water studies, and unfinished commissions of a man who found everything interesting. The argument is that his genius was curiosity plus observation, which makes it feel almost learnable.

books.title: The Operator: Firing the Shots That Killed Osama Bin Laden and My Years as a SEAL Team Warrior
books.author: Robert O'Neill
books.blurb: Robert O'Neill's account of four hundred combat missions, ending with the shot that killed bin Laden, and of what those years cost everyone involved. A blunt, first-person view of the SEAL machine.

books.title: Alexander Hamilton
books.author: Ron Chernow
books.blurb: The immigrant orphan who wrote his way into the revolution, built the American financial system, and died in a duel he probably let happen. Chernow's biography is the one that inspired the musical, and it's even better than that suggests.

books.title: Lincoln
books.author: David Herbert Donald
books.blurb: Donald's classic one-volume Lincoln: the ambitious prairie lawyer who grew into the presidency in real time, improvising through catastrophe. The standard against which Lincoln biographies get measured.

books.title: High Price: A Neuroscientist's Journey of Self-Discovery That Challenges Everything You Know About Drugs and Society
books.author: Carl Hart
books.blurb: Hart grew up in one of Miami's roughest neighborhoods and became a Columbia neuroscientist studying drugs, concluding that most of what America believes about addiction is wrong. Memoir and science interleaved, both aimed at the drug war.

books.title: Pimp: The Story of My Life
books.author: Iceberg Slim
books.blurb: Iceberg Slim's unflinching memoir of twenty-five years in the Chicago street life, written in the language of it. Brutal and unromantic; it influenced generations of writers and musicians precisely because it refuses to glamorize what it describes.

books.title: Educated: A Memoir
books.author: Tara Westover
books.blurb: Westover grew up in a survivalist Mormon family that didn't believe in school or doctors, and clawed her way from a junkyard childhood to a Cambridge PhD. A memoir about how education both frees you and costs you your family.

books.title: Elon Musk: Tesla, SpaceX, and the Quest for a Fantastic Future
books.author: Ashlee Vance
books.blurb: Vance's 2015 biography, written when Tesla and SpaceX were still plausible failures, remains the best account of Musk's early arc: PayPal, near-bankruptcy in 2008, and the will-it-into-existence style that built both companies.

books.title: How to Win Friends & Influence People
books.author: Dale Carnegie
books.blurb: Carnegie's 1936 manual on getting along with people: be genuinely interested, remember names, avoid arguments, let others save face. Corny on the surface, but the underlying observation that people run on feeling important has not aged a day.

books.title: Law School for Everyone
books.author: The Great Courses
books.blurb: A Great Courses series that walks through the first-year law curriculum: torts, contracts, criminal law, and civil procedure, taught by four law professors. The fastest way to understand how lawyers actually think.

books.title: The Republic
books.author: Plato
books.blurb: Plato's dialogue on justice, featuring the philosopher-kings, the noble lie, and the cave. The questions it asks about who should rule and why remain unresolved 2,400 years later, which is either depressing or reassuring.

books.title: 48 Laws of Power
books.author: Robert Greene
books.blurb: Greene distills history's manipulators into 48 amoral laws: conceal your intentions, never outshine the master, crush your enemy totally. Read it as a playbook or as a defense manual; either way you'll recognize your workplace in it.

books.title: Heads in Beds: A Reckless Memoir of Hotels, Hustles, and So-Called Hospitality
books.author: Jacob Tomsky
books.blurb: A decade in hotels, from luxury valet to front-desk burnout, with all the tips, scams, and upgrade levers explained by someone who worked them. Funny, and genuinely useful the next time you check in.

books.title: Never Split the Difference: Negotiating as if Your Life Depended on It
books.author: Chris Voss
books.blurb: Voss spent years as the FBI's lead hostage negotiator, and his toolkit transfers: tactical empathy, mirroring, calibrated questions, and getting to 'that's right.' The most practical negotiation book available, because none of it assumes goodwill.

books.title: 400 Things Cops Know: Street-Smart Lessons From a Veteran Patrolman
books.author: Adam Plantinga
books.blurb: A veteran patrol sergeant lists what the job teaches in 400 blunt observations, from how people lie to what a traffic stop feels like from the other side. A street-level education in how policing actually works.

books.title: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up: The Japanese Art of Decluttering and Organizing
books.author: Marie Kondo
books.blurb: Kondo's method is really a filter: hold each thing you own and keep it only if it sparks joy, category by category, clothes before mementos. Underneath the tidying is a fairly radical idea about deciding what your life is for.

books.title: Law 101: Everything You Need to Know About American Law
books.author: Jay M. Feinman
books.blurb: Feinman covers the first year of law school in one book: constitutional law, torts, contracts, property, and criminal procedure, with real cases as illustrations. The single most useful primer for understanding American legal news.

books.title: Arrest-Proof Yourself, Second Edition
books.author: Dale C. Carson
books.blurb: A former FBI agent turned defense lawyer explains how arrests actually happen, why so many are avoidable, and exactly how to behave in police encounters to stay out of the system. Uncomfortable, practical knowledge.
